title: Fix migration_test.dart and hebrew_migration_test.dart to exercise UserDatabase's real onUpgrade

evidence.quote: group('Schema migration v23→v24: Hebrew stage names', () {

why: Neither test actually drives UserDatabase.migration. migration_test.dart's group is titled 'v15 to v16' but user_database.dart's onUpgrade has no `if (from < 16)` block (only from<25 onward exists) — the test just creates a fresh onCreate'd v32 database via createTestDatabase() and asserts current column defaults, never running an upgrade. hebrew_migration_test.dart is worse: it hand-copies the English-to-Hebrew stage-name UPDATE statements into a local _runHebrewMigration helper and calls that — there is no `if (from < 24)` block in onUpgrade for it to call instead, so the helper is entirely disconnected from production migration code. Both give the false impression that UserDatabase's historical migrations are regression-tested; neither would catch a real regression, and neither caught the gap in finding 1.
recommendation: Either rebuild these as genuine migration tests using Drift's SchemaVerifier (open an old-schema fixture DB, call verifier.migrateAndValidate(db, 32), assert data survives) once drift_schemas/ exists per DB-4, or rename/rescope them honestly as current-schema behavior tests and delete the misleading version-number titles and the hand-copied SQL helper.
acceptance_criteria: Either the test constructs a real old-schema Drift database and runs it through UserDatabase's actual MigrationStrategy, or the file/group name no longer claims to test a migration version that doesn't exist in onUpgrade.
A red-first check: breaking the Hebrew-name mapping in production code (if/when it's reintroduced) fails this test; today nothing in production feeds it.
